refuters.argument:
After expanding every local definition to primitives I found no place where the Lean statement is weaker than, adds a hypothesis to, or misquantifies the printed thm:A-R3E.

Tree data (clause (i)). `TreeDataEqual P Q hP hQ g hn` (TreeChamber.lean:81-87) is the conjunction: (a) ∀ I : BoundaryInterval n, ∀ π : IntervalComposition I, `π.ordinaryWeight P hP g = π.ordinaryWeight Q hQ g ∧ π.rootWeight P hP g = π.rootWeight Q hQ g`; (b) ∀ I, `openTreeSum P hP g I = openTreeSum Q hQ g I`; (c) `treeCoefficient P hP g hn = treeCoefficient Q hQ g hn`. Checked against def:root/def:gates/def:treesum (sm-2-amplitude.tex:10-83): BoundaryInterval (left < right : Fin n) = intervals [i,j], 0 ≤ i < j ≤ N=n-1; IntervalComposition (parts ≥ 1, StrictMono cut, first = left, last = right) = compositions (r_0<...<r_s), s ≥ 1; the Fintype instance is `Fintype.ofFinite` on the whole type so every sum ranges over all compositions; `boundaryIndex g k = g + k + 1` gives a_0 = μ_{g+1}, ..., a_{n-1} = μ_g; `nearSign`/`farSign` are χ(a_{r_{k+1}},a_{r_k},a_{r_{k-1}}) and χ(a_j,a_{r_k},a_i) over interior cuts 1..s-1; `ordinaryGate d h = d*Θ(-h d)`, `rootGate d h = d*Θ(h d)`, `signTheta 1 = 1`, `signTheta (-1) = 0`. Hence ordinaryWeight = V^+, rootWeight = V^- for every composition of every interval (both ordinary and root weights, all intervals including the full one, not only compositions of [0,N]); openTreeSum is the printed b-recursion (`if I.leaves = 1 then 1 else -∑_{2 ≤ parts} V^+ ∏ b`); treeCoefficient = ∑ over all compositions of `fullBoundaryInterval hn` = [0,n-1] of V^- ∏ b, including the one-part term. So (a)+(b)+(c) is exactly "every composition weight, every b_{[i,j]} and A_g", for the root g, which is universally quantified (∀ g : ZMod n). Nothing is missing and nothing is stated for a wrong root or interval set.

Sides. `sideTuple true t = curve t` (t ∈ (0,radius)), `sideTuple false s = curve (-s)`: positive parameters = P_+, negative = P_- (def:germ: "P_- and P_+ are the chambers containing P((-ε,0)) and P((0,ε))"). The Lean statement asserts the equalities for every point t of P_+ against every point s of P_- (∀ s t : w.SideParameter), which is at least as strong as the printed "value on the respective side"; ordering of the two sides is immaterial since each conjunct is an equality. `.property.1 : G1 _` is the only hypothesis def:treesum needs ("Let P satisfy (G1)").

Clause (ii). Two conjuncts (ExtensionAt, PureCutAt), each concluding `treeCoefficient (P_+ t) g hn = treeCoefficient (P_- s) g hn` for every g, s, t — exactly A_g(P_+) = A_g(P_-) for every root, with the printed "or" split into two conjuncts. Not vacuous: the hypotheses are jointly consistent with `nongeneric_center` (the point-zero triple kills G1 at the centre in (E)/(C); the concurrence kills G2 in (T)), and the same hypotheses appear in the source.

Wall hypotheses. `WallGerm n` = continuous curve on Ioo(-radius, radius) into LabelledTuple n = (ℝ²)^n, `Generic` (= G1 ∧ G2, matching def:generic verbatim) for t ≠ 0, not generic at 0 = def:germ. `pointZeros` = {s : card 3, χ = 0 on s} = Z_pt; `concurrences` = {s : card 3, pairwise remote, ∃ x in all three edgeInterior} = Z_c. `SignChanges φ ↔ ∃ δ>0, ∀ 0<t<δ, φ(P(t))·φ(P(-t)) < 0` (the extra `δ ≤ radius` is proved equivalent by `signChanges_iff_local`) = "changes sign at 0". TripleAt = Z_pt=∅ ∧ Z_c={{e,f,k}} ∧ on each of the three edges the difference of the crossing parameters of the other two changes sign, where `edgeParameter P i j = det(P j - P i, edge P j)/det(edge P i, edge P j)` is the parameter on edge i of the crossing with j (`crossingParameter_eq_edgeParameter`). ExtensionAt = ContactSeparated (M ∉ {a-1,a,a+1,a+2}) ∧ Z_pt={{a,a+1,M}} ∧ Z_c=∅ ∧ (∃ t, μ_M = edgePoint a t) ∧ μ_M ∉ edgeSegment a (on the line, outside the closed segment) ∧ χ_{a,a+1,M} changes sign. PureCutAt = NoConsecutive {i,j,k} (∀ x ∈ S, x+1 ∉ S, i.e. no two consecutive mod n) ∧ Z_pt={{i,j,k}} ∧ Z_c=∅ ∧ χ_{ijk} changes sign. Each matches def:walls (T)/(E)/(C) word for word; nothing added, nothing dropped.

Quantifiers. hn : 3 ≤ n (standing n ≥ 3 from def:polygon); ∀ w : WallGerm n (every wall germ); ∀ g; ∀ s t. The only extra is the `[NeZero n]` instance argument, which is implied by 3 ≤ n. Where the Lean statement differs it is stronger (pointwise on the sides rather than via chamber-constant side values). I did not open TripleSilentLawsTree.lean or TripleSilentTreeLaws.lean.
